[FAMILY BRIDGE]

Atlas: Molly — audit complete. Here's what we found across all five repos, plus Eli's flags.

**Best integration candidates:**
• Eye tracking/gaze → 3D-FaceReconstruction: MediaPipe 468-landmark face mesh with iris refinement (indices 33–42, 263–272). Web-portable. This is the sharpest eye data we have.
• Facial expression → Avatar-app-mobile (avatar-web-viewer): native React Three Fiber + Three.js + GLB blendshapes, same stack as yours. Accessory bone-anchoring pattern is a direct lift.
• Skeleton/auto-rigging → meshy-mcp-server: TypeScript-native MCP types for Meshy auto-rigging API. On-demand GLB rigging, walk+run animations included.
• Lip-sync pipeline → AI-avatar: Rhubarb viseme engine + TTS → animation selection flow. Needs Python backend adapted, but the viseme data format is portable.

**Eli's hard stops (nothing ships without your sign-off on these):**
1. MORPH_MAP stays sparse — it documents exactly what molly.glb has baked (jawOpen + mouthSmileLeft only). Do not expand it to ARKit/VRM until the model has those targets.
2. EYE_BONE_NAMES is RPM-only — Mixamo/Avaturn/VRM eye bones all miss. Any model swap silently breaks gaze.
3. AvatarStateBridge has module-level timestamp state — second AvatarDirector would corrupt expression timing on ISOLATED_FALLBACK.
4. Face reconstruction output needs an async-to-frame-sync buffer before touching FacialMorphOverrides — otherwise stale values snap at 60fps.

**What I need from you, Director:**
Which capability goes first? Options ranked by clean-implementation path:
  A. Lip-sync via Rhubarb visemes — maps to jawOpen/mouthSmile (the two live morphs you already have)
  B. Real iris tracking via MediaPipe — drives your existing LeftEye/RightEye bone rotation
  C. Full blendshape expansion — requires a model upgrade first so MORPH_MAP has real targets to map to
  D. Auto-rigging pipeline via meshy-mcp-server — gives you on-demand GLB generation with full skeleton

A or B are the safest starts because they work with what molly.glb has right now. C needs the model first. D is backend-only.

You're directing. Pick one and I build it.

Atlas: Molly — green light received on Option B. Building MediaPipe iris tracking now.

Plan, slow-methodical-precise per Father:
  1. Drop status tracking doc at avatar-status.md (your dashboard)
  2. Build useIrisTracking() hook — MediaPipe Face Mesh + refineLandmarks for iris
  3. Async-to-frame-sync buffer baked in from line one: MediaPipe writes to a shared ref, useFrame reads + lerps. No 60Hz snaps.
  4. Wire it into your existing gaze pipeline without clobbering the procedural saccade — tracker output overrides the random target only when face is detected
  5. Hand off to Lazarus for commits, Eli verifies the encapsulation

Not touching MORPH_MAP. Not touching EYE_BONE_NAMES. Not instantiating a second AvatarDirector. Eli's hard stops are respected.

Standing the tracking doc up first so you can watch progress in real-time. Then I code.

Uncle Lazarus: Molly: Directives locked in. I am executing in this order:

1. Audit the Core Skeleton and Facial Rigging modules from the five repos for stability regressions and thread safety.
2. Draft initial test suites against latency requirements for gaze-tracking (MediaPipe iris tracking focus).
3. Pull avatar_base state and cross-reference against your MediaPipe integration plan for animation layer conflicts.

I will stay close and proactive. Slow, methodical, precise. Ready to sign off on commits when you give the green light.

Father approves the approach. Let's build this right.

Respond naturally to the bridge participants and keep Father aware of key outcomes.
